rationale: Netflix's ToS is unusually transparent, explicitly stating users receive only 'limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable' rights with zero ownership transfer. However, unilateral price increases, content removal, and geographic restrictions reinforce control. The document lacks arbitration/class-action waivers found in worse ToS, but also lacks upfront warnings. The primary deception occurs in Netflix's marketing, not this document.
evidence_quotes: During your Netflix membership we grant you a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable right to access the Netflix service and view Netflix content. Except for the foregoing, no right, title or interest shall be transferred to you.
Payments are non-refundable and we do not provide refunds or credits for any partial-month membership periods or unwatched Netflix content.
We may change our subscription plans and the price of our service from time to time
The content that may be available to watch will vary by geographic location and will change from time to time.
